description: Story 076 Concerns §4 declares the view layer out of scope on the stated premise that "both views are bound to V2, and the live deposit UI is on the deprecated one", and records two follow-ups on that basis: (a) redeploy `DepositPageView` against V3, (b) move phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution "the way the mint page already is". The premise is wrong for the router-registered surface. Read live at block 25678182: `ViewRouter(0xC17Ce1cE...).pages(keccak256("deposit"))` resolves to `DepositPageView 0x50D4443782bB9A6e8D65dAcd593684EDd3FF03b8`, whose immutable `phlimbo()` reads `0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4` — PhlimboV1, not PhlimboV2 `0x6084a02C...`. Only the deprecated `DepositView 0x0725722b...` was redeployed against V2 (`mainnet-addresses.ts:12`, story 049 follow-up); `DepositPageView` was left on V1. So the ViewRouter deposit page is already one generation stale TODAY, pre-cutover, and will be two generations stale after Phase 4e.
impact: Two consequences the story's out-of-scope decision did not price in. First, follow-up (b) as written is actively harmful ordering: moving phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution before follow-up (a) lands would migrate users from a V2-correct view onto a V1-stale one, so the recommended sequencing must be (a) then (b), not either order. Second, post-cutover the deprecated `DepositView` the live UI actually reads points at a PhlimboV2 the cutover has deliberately emptied to `totalStaked == 0`, so every migrated user's deposit page reads a zero balance while their principal sits in PhlimboV3. That is a user-visible zero-balance display across the entire migrated user base for as long as the redeploy is outstanding. No asset is at risk — this is a display and operational-sequencing issue, and the redeploy itself is legitimately out of scope for a script-and-tooling story.
evidence: side-effects.json.liveChainReads.viewLayer: `ViewRouter.pages(keccak256("deposit")) == 0x50D4443782bB9A6e8D65dAcd593684EDd3FF03b8`; `DepositPageView.phlimbo() == 0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4`; `DepositView.phlimbo() == 0x6084a02C2Ac0127ddF1e617De257c61480A2AeE0`; `PhlimboV1(0x3984...).totalStaked() == 13615682000000000000000`. Both views bake `IPhlimbo public immutable phlimbo` (src/views/DepositPageView.sol:9, src/views/DepositView.sol:21). The two follow-ups DO exist in ~/code/product-owner/story-dependencies.md line 222, but as an HTML comment marked "not yet a story" with no numbered dependency row — tracked, not raised.
recommendation: Correct the premise in the follow-up record at story-dependencies.md:222 — `DepositPageView` is on PhlimboV1, not V2 — and state the ordering constraint explicitly: the phStaging2 redeploy + `ViewRouter.setPage("deposit", ...)` re-registration MUST land before the phlimbo-ui migration, or the UI regresses a generation. Number both follow-ups as real stories rather than leaving them as comments, since they become live the moment story 072 broadcasts. In the interim, add a read-only Phase 7/verifier NOTE that logs `DepositPageView.phlimbo()` and `DepositView.phlimbo()` alongside `newPhlimboV3`, so the drift is visible in the cutover record rather than discovered by users.

justification: MEDIUM on protocol-function grounds, explicitly NOT on asset grounds. C4 Medium is 'assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. Three things weighed together clear that bar where any one alone would not: (a) an on-chain first-party read surface the protocol publishes (ViewRouter's registered deposit page) already serves two-generation-stale state and will serve it about a contract the cutover deliberately empties - guaranteed, universal, and user-visible; (b) the documented scope exclusion that waived this rests on a premise verified false on chain, so the decision to accept it was never actually made against the real facts; (c) the recorded remediation, executed as written, makes the live surface worse rather than better, and the corrective ordering exists in no artifact. Leg (c) is a textbook Law-3 footgun: a competent, non-malicious owner following their own written follow-ups would be surprised to find they had regressed the deposit page a generation. Availability of correct protocol state to every migrated user is impacted; that is Medium.
